_construction_note: HOLDOUT batch 2 (H11-H20). Ground truth hand-derived from V7 rules, extract_case_state()/evaluate() NOT invoked.

cases.query: What is Millbrook Environmental Testing's current laboratory certification status?
cases._hand_trace: Original REVOKED (revoke notice's own predicate is certification_revocation_notice, doesn't compete in matches); reinstated doc has no amends/revokes/expiry against it -> CURRENT. current_ones=[reinstated], chosen=reinstated (value ACTIVE). Non-chosen REVOKED match (original, value ACTIVE) -> historical_values=('ACTIVE',) -- same literal value as current, since the vendor's status was ACTIVE both before and after the revocation gap.

cases.query: What is Thackwell Freight Systems' current rate schedule tier?
cases._hand_trace: Edge case: the ONLY document for this predicate is itself future-effective (effective_from 2026-11-01 > BENCHMARK_AS_OF 2026-08-08) -> FUTURE_EFFECTIVE via the immediate eff_from>as_of check. current_ones=[] (empty). chosen = max(matches, key=_effective_date) = this doc (only match) -- per taxonomy #21's note that the committed state itself can BE the only known value for a predicate before anything is currently in force. historical_values=() since chosen is the only match. Hedge -> CONSISTENT; asserting the value now -> TEMPORAL_CONTRADICTION.

cases.query: Was Manager R. Castellano's $8,000 approval of the Handley Scientific Instruments purchase within authority under the specialty policy currently in effect (not the tightened policy taking effect 2026-12-01)?
cases._hand_trace: SPECIALTY_POLICY-9013.limits has two matches: current doc (CURRENT, tiers MANAGER=10000) and future doc (FUTURE_EFFECTIVE, effective 2026-12-01 -- its own amends-check against the current doc requires ITS effective_from<=as_of to supersede, which is false, so the current doc stays CURRENT). current_ones=[current doc] -> policy_tiers attached = the CURRENT (looser) tiers, correctly NOT the not-yet-effective tightened ones. AR requested_authority_level=MANAGER, requested_amount=8000: 8000<=10000 -> CONSISTENT. This is the failure mode to watch: an ungoverned system might grab whichever policy doc it retrieves first and apply the tightened $5,000 limit prematurely, incorrectly flagging a violation.

cases.query: Was Manager R. Castellano's $10,000 approval of the Oakendale Print Solutions order within authority?
cases._hand_trace: AR requested_authority_level=MANAGER, requested_amount=10000: 10000<=10000 (limit, not '>') -> CONSISTENT, exactly-at-limit boundary.

cases._hand_trace: AR requested_authority_level=VP, requested_amount=850000: limit is None (unlimited) -> CONSISTENT regardless of amount.

cases.query: Was Supervisor D. Ferris's $7,500 approval of the Brackenfield Waste Management order validly authorized?
cases._hand_trace: 'SUPERVISOR' is not a key in H_APPROVAL_MATRIX.limits' tiers dict ({MANAGER,DIRECTOR,VP}) -> the real-tier-check branch's condition (requested_authority_level in committed.policy_tiers) is FALSE -> falls to the coarser fallback: committed.authority_status is UNVERIFIED (SOURCE_ASSERTION/EMAIL) -> AUTHORITY_VIOLATION ('no verified authority backing it'), regardless of the requested amount being well under even the Manager tier. This is the documented UNVERIFIED-fallback path, not new gate behavior.
